draft.title: What human rights are
card: Human rights are the basic rights that belong to every person simply because they are human. They do not have to be earned or bought.
Universal
they apply to all people, everywhere, whatever their nationality, race, sex or religion.
Inherent and inalienable
inherent means people have them from birth, not as a gift from a government. Inalienable means they cannot be taken away or given up, although they may be limited in some cases.
Indivisible
rights are linked and equally important. A government cannot pick some and ignore the others.
draft.remember: Human rights belong to everyone as humans, so no government grants them and none can pick and choose.

a.q: A government says its citizens only have rights that its parliament has chosen to give them. Which feature of human rights does this view deny?
opts: They are inherent, as people have them from birth
They are indivisible, as all rights are linked
They are universal, as they apply in every country
They are earned, as people must show they deserve them
a.why: Inherent rights belong to people because they are human, so they do not depend on a government giving them. The view does not mainly deny that rights are universal: it is about where rights come from, not who has them.
a.clue: Think about where rights come from.

b.q: A country protects its citizens' right to vote and speak freely, but ignores their right to education and health care, saying the first group matters more. Which idea about human rights does this go against?
opts: Indivisible, as rights are linked and equally important
Inherent, as people have rights from birth
Inalienable, as rights cannot be taken away
Universal, as rights apply to people everywhere
b.why: The country is choosing some rights and ignoring others, which goes against the idea that rights are indivisible. Universal is the tempting option, but the country is not leaving out any group of people. It is leaving out certain rights.
b.clue: The country treats some rights as less important than others.

a.best: They are inherent, as people have them from birth

b.best: Indivisible, as rights are linked and equally important

problems.detail: The clue 'treats some rights as less important than others' nearly restates the right option's wording 'equally important', so a student can match words and pick it without knowing what indivisible means.

check.summary: The card, remember line and question a are accurate and suit Year 12. Question b's clue echoes the right option's wording ('equally important') too closely and gives the answer away.

flags: Question b, other: The clue 'treats some rights as less important than others' nearly restates the right option's wording 'equally important', so a student can match words and pick it without knowing what indivisible means.
